Thanks Sofia — good notes. Internal recap for the team + proposed action items before the engineering kickoff. I copied Karthik and Ben for technical ownership. High-level answers below; Karthik will add specifics and an ops checklist.

Summary answers (short):
- Vector dims: recommend starting at 512 for your catalog size (10M rows) — good balance: better recall than 384, modest increase in storage/compute vs 1024. We can run a quick A/B sample to confirm.
- Auth/routing: for AeroMart we can support hybrid routing. Private VPC for PII/transactional queries; hosted Redwood endpoints for non-PII read-only embeddings/semantic search. We'll provide the routing policy config you can apply in our console and a sample IAM/KMS mapping for the private control plane.
- Batching & normalization: client-side L2 normalization is fine (we accept normalized and non-normalized vectors), but if you plan to use cosine similarity in your search stack, normalize on ingest. For near-real-time (5s) we suggest micro-batching of up to 256 vectors or an adaptive window capped at 2s — tradeoffs below.

Proposed action items (owners & timeline):
1) Karthik — produce an "Embed cutover checklist" with: dim/quantization recommendation, sample A/B plan, expected storage/cost delta (2 business days).
2) Ben — prepare auth/routing template (VPC peering + fallback hosted routing rules + KMS key mapping). Add how to configure the routing policy in the Redwood Console (2 business days).
3) Marissa / Connor — finalize commercial scope (which endpoints are private vs hosted) and expected committed qps for sizing (EOD Thu).
4) Internal / AeroMart joint: run sample export of 10k rows for A/B (norm vs non-norm) — target next Tue.

Karthik / Ben — flag any blockers. I attached our starter embed profile (redwood_embed_profile_v1.json) to map fields.

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + a couple of integration questions

Adding technical detail as promised — tried to be pragmatic for a first cut. Notes below are focused on the embedding side (dims, batching, normalization, migration).

1) Dim recommendation rationale- 512 dims: expected to increase per-vector storage by ~33% vs 384 but gives a clear uplift on recall for short product descriptions. 1024 dims can help for long-form content and multimodal signals, but we'd advise 512 for initial cutover to limit cost. We can run an offline retrieval eval on a 50k sample and measure recall@10.

2) Batching guidance (ingest)
- Latency target 5s: use an adaptive micro-batching approach. Default config: 2s window OR 256 vectors whichever comes first. That keeps median push latency ~1.8s for typical payloads and maintains GPU utilization.
- Throughput tuning: if you plan periodic bulk reindex (nightly), we recommend larger batches (1k-4k) with transient higher throughput nodes (we can help schedule Dedicated bursts).

3) Normalization & similarity metric- If your search uses cosine similarity, normalize vectors before storage. Redwood supports both normalized and raw vectors; our similarity layer will do the right thing if you mark the index type. For migration from provider-X (your current): export vectors and metadata; we recommend re-embedding a small stratified sample (~5-10k) to check distribution drift. If distributions diverge, re-embedding is preferable to relying solely on mapping.

4) Migration plan (high level)
- Phase 0: sample extraction (5–10k stratified) + offline evaluation (2–3 days).
- Phase 1: pilot ingest (100k) into a non-prod index with 512 dims, evaluate recall, latency, cost (7 days).
- Phase 2: cutover per-namespace with canary traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%), rollback policy if eval metric drop >5%.

5) SDK & auth notes
- SDKs: we have language SDKs that handle batch helper functions and L2 normalization snippets. For private VPC, auth is mTLS with KMS-backed signing; for hybrid routing you can issue short-lived tokens for hosted calls while keeping long-lived service principals for private traffic. I'll drop code snippets to the Drive link.

Open questions for AeroMart (please confirm):
- Do you plan to store product images metadata with vectors or separate? That affects per-vector payload size.
- Is there an internal requirement for absolute determinism of vectors across re-embeds (same seed/model) or do you prefer periodic refreshes?

I'll draft the Embed cutover checklist today and put it in the Drive folder.

—Karthik
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
